🤝 Iraq reaches deal with Kataib Hezbollah — without the US Iraq’s government has reached a last-minute agreement with Kataib Hezbollah instead of forcing the militia out of a key town south of Baghdad it has controlled since 2014, according to Al Jazeera. 🔴 Officials had accused the group of stealing hundreds of millions in state oil. 🔴 Facing threats of armed resistance and intervention by Iran’s Quds Force commander, Baghdad opted for a compromise rather than a confrontation. 🔴 The deal establishes a shared security presence starting tomorrow afternoon, mixing army, police, and militia fighters under a new command. Iraqi government didn't get a total military victory—the militia keeps its role. ⚡️ French President Emmanuel Macron said Ukraine’s NATO membership should be reconsidered amid Russia’s maximalist demands, arguing that the country’s future military strength and NATO membership would serve Europe’s long-term security. “Given the current circumstances, where we are facing maximalist positions from Russia, the issue of Ukraine’s NATO membership must be raised again. This is precisely what I proposed a few days ago. Now is the right moment for this,” Macron said. He added that Ukraine would emerge from the war with a powerful arsenal and a large army, making its presence in NATO a matter of long-term European security. Macron also outlined the proposed sequence for negotiations involving Ukraine, the U.S., Europe, and Russia: first, establish security guarantees for Ukraine; then address territorial issues; and finally discuss a peace agreement. According to Macron, the substance of Ukraine’s security guarantees was already finalized in January with the participation of U.S. representatives. He also noted that Moscow had yet to present any concrete peace proposals.
